body.statement: As \(u\to\infty\), \(\Pr\{D(0)>u,R_{\mathrm c}(0)>R(u)\}=o\{\Delta(u)\lambda(u)\}\), \(\lambda(u)>0\), and \(\mathfrak L(u)\ne\varnothing\) eventually. There are unique universal constants \(\beta_{\star}>0\), \(\gamma_{\star}\in\mathbb R\), and \(c_{\star}\in\mathbb R\) such that \(\mathcal E_{\star}(u)=\beta_{\star}u+\gamma_{\star}\log u+c_{\star}\in\mathfrak E\), \(-\log\lambda(u)=\mathcal E_{\star}(u)+o(1)\), and \(\lambda(u+x)/\lambda(u)\to e^{-\beta_{\star}x}\) uniformly for \(x\) in each compact subset of \(\mathbb R\). In the exact uniform regime \(\ell(u)\in\mathfrak L(u)=[u^3,\lambda(u)^{-1/2}]\), \(\sup_{\ell\in\mathfrak L(u)}|\Pr\{\sup_{0\le t\le\ell}D(t)>u\}/\{\ell\lambda(u)\}-1|\to0\). The expansion implies \(\mathcal E_{\star}'(u)>0\) for every \(u\ge u_0\), so the displayed definitions of \(b(T)\) and positive \(a(T)\) are valid only on \([T_0,\infty)\). As \(T\to\infty\) through this domain, and hence eventually with \(u_{\mathrm p}(T)\ge u_0\), \(\mathcal N_T\) converges to a Poisson random measure with intensity \(dt\,e^{-x}dx\), and \(\Pr\{[M_T-b(T)]/a(T)\le x\}\to\exp\{-e^{-x}\}\). The padded grid target obeys \(\{M_T^{\mathrm{sim}}-M_T\}/a(T)\to0\) in probability on the same eventual domain. These growing-domain assertions strictly strengthen the one-location Brownian--GCM LR law of Banerjee and Wellner (2001), recovered at \(D(0)\).
body.justification: This is the theorem-level kernel: simultaneous LR calibration requires the rare-event law of the LR energy field, not the fixed-point law.
body.gap: Banerjee and Wellner (2001) give \(D(0)\); Hooghiemstra and Lopuhaä (1998) and Durot, Kulikov, and Lopuhaä (2012) give extremes for argmax or slope error, not for \(D\).
body.consumer: No analytic or simulated simultaneous critical value should be justified from this theorem until the sharp cluster law and grid approximation are proved.

obligation.what_is_open: The infinite-domain small-noise principle, sharp one-cluster expansion, additive tail ratio, positive runs intensity, uniform rare-block law, short-range anticlustering, marked Poisson limit, Gumbel law, and growing-window padding and mesh approximation remain unproved.
obligation.obstruction: Exact Brownian scaling and a variational action bracket do not yield the translation-mode prefactor or constant-order logarithmic-tail accuracy. Long-range truncation does not imply short-range anticlustering, and no frozen or cited theorem supplies the peak-mark law for this nonlinear Brownian--GCM energy field.
obligation.attempted: The exact small-noise scaling, Hilbert-projection action lower bound, and compactly supported plateau witness with unit LR energy and action nine-eighths were checked equation by equation. These calculations identify the candidate speed and a nontrivial action bracket but stop before any sharp probability asymptotic.
obligation.partial_result:
Let \(\Phi(h)\) be the origin-constrained LR energy generated by \(t^2+h(t)\), for an absolutely continuous \(h\) with \(h(0)=0\) and \(h'\in L^2(\mathbb R)\).  For \(b>0\), define \(h_b(t)=b^2h(t/b)\).  Spatial and affine equivariance of the constrained and unrestricted GCMs, followed by the substitution \(t=bs\), give the exact homogeneities
\[
 \Phi(h_b)=b^3\Phi(h),
 \qquad
 \frac12\int_{\mathbb R}h_b'(t)^2\,dt
 =b^3\frac12\int_{\mathbb R}h'(t)^2\,dt.
\]
Brownian scaling with \(b=u^{1/3}\) therefore yields the exact identity
\[
 \Pr\{D(0)>u\}
 =\Pr\{\Phi(u^{-1/2}\mathbb W)>1\}.
\]
Thus \(u\), rather than a power inferred from an analogy with slope extremes, is the candidate small-noise speed.

Define the deterministic action
\[
 I_\star=inf\left\{
  \frac12\int_{\mathbb R}h'(t)^2\,dt:\Phi(h)\ge1
 \right\}.
\]
On a finite interval containing the contact set, let \(\mathcal C_0\subset\mathcal C\) be the zero-constrained and unrestricted monotone-slope cones.  Since the baseline slope \(2t\) belongs to \(\mathcal C_0\), the Hilbert projection identity gives
\[
 \Phi(h)
 =\operatorname{dist}^2(2t+h',\mathcal C_0)
  -\operatorname{dist}^2(2t+h',\mathcal C)
 \le\|h'\|_2^2.
\]
After increasing the finite interval through the stabilized contact set, this proves \(I_\star\ge1/2\).

For the converse deterministic witness, put \(k=4^{1/3}\), \(a=k/4\), and
\[
 h'(t)=(k-2t)\mathbf 1\{-a\le t\le k/2\}.
\]
Then \(2t+h'(t)\) is nondecreasing and equals \(k\) on \([-a,k/2]\).  Its unrestricted isotonic projection is itself, while its zero-constrained projection replaces the plateau by zero on \([-a,0]\).  Hence
\[
 \Phi(h)=ak^2=\frac{k^3}{4}=1
\]
and, by direct integration,
\[
 \frac12\int_{\mathbb R}h'(t)^2\,dt
 =\frac12\int_{-a}^{k/2}(k-2t)^2\,dt
 =\frac{(k+2a)^3}{12}
 =\frac98.
\]
Therefore
\[
 \frac12\le I_\star\le\frac98.
\]
The same witness is compactly supported, so finite-window PAVA recovers it once the window contains \([-a,k/2]\).  These exact identities do not constitute an infinite-domain large-deviation principle.  Even such a principle would determine only a logarithmic rate; it would not determine the translation-mode prefactor, an additive \(o(1)\) expansion of \(-\log\lambda(u)\), the compact-additive tail ratio, short-range anticlustering, marked-Poisson convergence, or the padded-grid error.  In particular, none of those conclusions follows from stationarity or from the action bracket.
